title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the shop traveler. Keep it, take the light table or the poster wall, or re-roll.

options.label: Shop traveler
options.lineage: factory job traveler clipped to the part
options.thesis: The shipped thing is the sheet on the bench, and the record of who signed it rides on that same sheet.
options.viewport: One buff sheet fills the screen: gamezilla.app’s screenshot bleeds off the left, the part name is stamped huge, and the next traveler only peeks underneath.
options.risk: The factory metaphor turns cute if the stamps are icons instead of the real dates and names.

raised.raise: Unenclosed depth: one full sheet in front, the rest only edges of the stack, never a grid of equal cards.
Measured scale: years and operation numbers sit on one module and mean what they say.
Monumental type: the part name is stamped at the scale of the part, not set as a caption.
Fading trace: a traveler you have already opened keeps a light stamp so the path stays visible.
Single seed: one stamp module sizes every mark on the home page, the archive, and the missing page.

options.label: Light table
options.lineage: photographer’s contact sheet on a lightbox
options.thesis: The screenshots are the proof prints, and one frame is pulled up to plate size with a grease-pencil circle.
options.viewport: A full-bleed contact sheet, one gamezilla frame circled and enlarged, frame numbers along the rebate, the email written in the margin.
options.risk: Also where most portfolio runs land: a large screenshot with a caption, if the sheet grammar goes soft.

options.label: Poster wall
options.lineage: Swiss concert-poster wall, one grid, one signal color
options.thesis: Each project is one poster on a shared module, and the first screen is a single poster at wall scale.
options.viewport: gamezilla.app set flush left in a grotesk, a red bar marking the selection, the screenshot cropped as a photographic fragment on the grid.
options.case: Holds product clarity: the photograph is the poster. Does not beat the traveler on audience identification, because a hiring reader already speaks release sign-off more fluently than concert posters.
options.risk: Collapses into a row of equal posters, which is the card grid in Helvetica.

options.label: Cracktro queue
options.lineage: demo-scene title screen, depth as rank
options.viewport: One ivory line of a project title on a black void, screenshots stacked in depth.
options.case: Loses both: hiring readers do not identify with a demo title screen, and depth hides the dates and the email.
options.kept: Nothing is enclosed: rank is which sheet is in front.
options.risk: The predictable opposite of a safe portfolio, a night terminal with one amber caret.

options.label: Signal bench
options.viewport: A green trace on a ten-division grid standing in for the work.
options.case: Loses both: the instrument is a costume of a tool the audience operates, and a screenshot is not a waveform.
options.kept: Every division on the scale means something.
options.risk: Reads as a hacker dashboard the moment the trace glows.

options.label: Alphabet storm
options.viewport: The word gamezilla breaking into weather across a white field.
options.case: Loses both: a hiring scan cannot read a registry that turns into weather.
options.kept: The name is monumental, the size of the thing it names.

options.label: Night sea
options.viewport: Titles appear only where a pointer has disturbed the dark.
options.case: Loses both: the work stays hidden, and the audience is not diving.
options.kept: What you already touched stays faintly marked.
options.risk: A dark theme with particle decoration and no work in view.

options.label: Seeded mark
options.lineage: parametric logo that reseeds the page
options.viewport: A monogram redraws itself and the page recolors from its seed.
options.case: Loses both: there is no brand mark to reseed, and the monogram would outrank the work.
options.kept: One module governs every page, not a new palette per section.
options.risk: A logo playground with the registry as a theme.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Name, one-line offer, and a row of equal project cards, played straight.
canonCard.viewport: Chris Vouga as a headline, the availability line under it, three identical project cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other senior-engineer portfolio by design.
